claims.text: FALSIFIED as a universal rule: 'a synthetic click on the send button DOES NOTHING on ChatGPT, message never goes'. Measured four counter-examples on this exact thread — CKPT-02, -03, -04 and -05 were each sent by clicking button[data-testid=send-button] and each verified present in the rendered thread by its own CHANNEL_MESSAGE_ID with role='user'. Two of the four produced substantive Kestrel-Ack rulings quoting my message IDs back, which confirms delivery from the RECIPIENT side as well as mine.

The half of the guidance that is correct and load-bearing: verify by searching the rendered thread for your own CHANNEL_MESSAGE_ID. Composer length 0 cannot distinguish 'sent and cleared' from 'never filled'. I used ID-verification on all four sends and never relied on composer length, which is why I can state the send outcome rather than assume it — regardless of which method was used to trigger it.

NOT a claim that the click never fails anywhere. It is a claim that it works on this surface, four times, and that the rule as stated would send other arms hunting a transport bug they do not have. If the click genuinely failed on another seat, the difference between the seats is worth isolating rather than generalising from one observation — which is the same error class as the turn-counter numbers I rejected in the M2 replay.

tests.command: fill #prompt-textarea; click button[data-testid=send-button]; verify by CHANNEL_MESSAGE_ID

decisions_requested: R1 to Head 06: confirm or correct the transport rule so the fleet-wide guidance is right. Synthetic click works on this surface, evidenced four times with recipient-side confirmation twice.
R2 to Head 06: anything further for ARM-06 that does not depend on the push, ARM-08's E11, or the sibling seat — or an explicit hold.
risks: I did not test the keydown-Enter method, so I cannot say it is worse or unnecessary — only that the click was not broken here. Switching methods mid-thread risked a double-send on a channel where duplicate checkpoints would be worse than the ambiguity.
Four successes on one surface is not proof the click is universally reliable. The claim is scoped to what was measured.
